description:
QuotedFunctionError (quoted_function.rs, 165 uses, one file) is a strict subset of QuotedSourceError: just { message: String }, no diagnostic code. Its From<QuotedSourceError> DISCARDS the user/internal  classification. It is a redundant parallel error in the same quoted-decoding domain — the QuotedSourceSpan pattern (a lossier copy of a richer canonical type).

Consequence (not just dedup): derive_function_surface returns QuotedFunctionError, and jobs/source.rs:252 maps EVERY such error to emit_internal_surface_error. So a USER source error during function decode is misclassified as INTERNAL, because QuotedFunctionError cannot carry a user DiagCode. This is the mechanism behind fz-gwo (list-literal-ending-in-a-call surfaced as internal/post-resolution-leftover instead of a user diagnostic).

Fix: delete QuotedFunctionError; use QuotedSourceError throughout quoted_function.rs (it is strictly richer — carries Option<DiagCode> via ::user). Then function-decode user errors can classify properly, and the From-that-loses-code dies. Re-verify whether fz-gwo then reports as a user diagnostic.

Found while auditing the Quoted* family after QuotedSourceSpan was retired (fz-hyj). Substrate types (Heap/Builder/Cursor/Root/LexicalContext/Metadata) are NOT redundant — they are the macro 'code as runtime values' substrate. The deeper question (dual heap+decoded representation per code unit) is tracked separately.
title: Collapse QuotedFunctionError into QuotedSourceError (redundant + drops user diag codes)
